# One subscription form reaches every signal

Three kinds of signal fire a cascade: success terminals, error-class terminals,
and per-key attribute-changed signals. A `subscribes` entry looks the same for
all three, so an author writing "react to X" does not need to know which kind X
belongs to.

## The template

```yaml
name: signal-blind-demo
version: "1"
nodes:
  - type: emitter
    kind: loop_counter
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max: {type: integer, default: 9}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: failer
    executor: http-node
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          url: {type: string, default: "http://127.0.0.1:9/unreachable"}

  - type: on_success
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: emitter
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {v: {type: integer, default: 1}}}

  - type: on_attribute
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: emitter
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {v: {type: integer, default: 1}}}

  - type: on_error
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: failer
        type: terminal/error/*
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {v: {type: integer, default: 1}}}

  - type: on_error_filtered
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: failer
        type: terminal/error/*
        force_upstream_refresh: false
        when: "type.startsWith('terminal/error/http')"
    attributes:
      schema: {type: object, properties: {v: {type: integer, default: 1}}}
```

`failer` points at an address nothing is listening on, so it emits
`terminal/error/http/network_error`.

## Drive it

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" -d '{}'

curl -sS "$BASE/v1/observability/events?instance_id=$IID&limit=500"
```

## What the product does

The run emits all three cascade-firing kinds — a success terminal, an error-class
terminal, and an attribute-changed signal. All four receivers dispatch exactly
once each.

Every subscription entry above uses the same keys: `node`, `type`,
`force_upstream_refresh`, plus the optional `when` predicate. No signal kind
needs a special form, and the wildcard and the predicate compose with the same
entry rather than replacing it.

## A signal that cannot fire is refused at registration

Transient signals are audit-only: they never fire a cascade. Subscribing to one
is refused when the template is registered, not discovered later by watching a
receiver that never wakes.

```yaml
nodes:
  - type: on_transient
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: emitter
        type: transient/park
        force_upstream_refresh: false
```

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/templates" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d "$SPEC"
# 400 — the error names transient/park and states that transient signals are audit-only
```
